failure_modes: Giving reusable sample functions, Hessian information or free y* changes the oracle and invalidates this information accounting.
Treating the inactive scalar coefficients as carrying no hidden-frame information bypasses the purpose of the genie.
Dropping the coercive wrapper permits escape outside the intended hard region.
Replacing bounded overlap by a sum over all scales can lose the stated variation budget.
This method record is not a reconstructible standalone Hard Family contract and must not be used as one.
content.goal_pattern: Turn sequential hidden-direction progress into raw fresh-SFO query lower bounds without a zero-respecting restriction or bounded query domain.
content.key_choice: Split the frontier residual into telescoping flattened resolutions, use matched normal widths, and compensate the lower lift so its exact response reproduces the wrapped hard objective. Reveal a scalar sample potential by independent Bernoulli draws and augment the transcript with all adaptive-span projections.
content.key_relation: For β=Cβ ε/(κL), T=floor(cT Δ/(Lβ²)), informative-gradient envelope B=Cμβ²/ϑ and p=B²/(σ_g²+B²), the source obtains T/p of order κ²LΔε^−2+ϑ²κ⁸σ_g²L³Δε^−6. This is a worked source application, not a generic transfer theorem.
proof_skeleton: A.1, p.11: use Ψ(t)=0 for t≤1/2 and exp(1−(2t−1)^−2) otherwise, Φ(t)=sqrt(e)∫_{−∞}^t exp(−s²/2)ds, chain components φ1=−Φ(z1), φi=Ψ(−z_{i−1})Φ(−zi)−Ψ(z_{i−1})Φ(zi). Scale H=ηLβ² Hhat_T(z/β). Flat tail masks h_i=e0(Σ_{j=i}^T c0(zj/β)²) define R0=ηLβ²Σφi(z/β)h_i, R=R0−R0(0), A=H−R. Lemma A.1 supplies bounded residual jets and prefix/next-coordinate support. Exact cutoff choices and their plateau conditions remain at equation (10).

A.2, p.12: choose Haar U∈R^{d×T}, Rrad=Kβsqrt(T), b(u)=u/sqrt(1+||u||²/Rrad²), P(u)=νRrad²(sqrt(1+||u||²/Rrad²)−1), ν=η0ηL. Set H_U=H(Uᵀb)+P, A_U=A(Uᵀb)+P. Lemma A.2 imports coercivity, gap O(TηLβ²), Lip(∇H_U)=O(L), and ||∇H_U||≥ηLβ/2 when |(Uᵀb(u))_T|<β; this prevents escaping through arbitrary large query magnitudes.

A.3, pp.12–14: flatten cδ(t)=tω(t/δ), Rδ=R(Cδ(z)); Lemma A.3 supplies derivative/localization estimates and annular separation. For 1≤ϑ≤κ choose J=floor(log_4(max{1,log ϑ})), a_j=1−4^{−j−1}, b_j=1−(1/2)4^{−j}, δ_j=c*βϑ^{−a_j}, w_j=c*βϑ^{−b_j}. Use E0=R if J=0; otherwise E0=Rδ0, Ej=Rδj−Rδ(j−1), EJ=R−Rδ(J−1). Their sum is R, at most three component jets overlap, and w_J is of order β/ϑ.

With r(u)=R(Uᵀb(u)), e_j(u)=E_j(Uᵀb(u)), q_w(s)=wq(s/w) for an odd compactly supported C³ q equal to identity on [−1/4,1/4], define K(u,s)=μr(u)²/(2L²)−(μ/L)Σe_j(u)q_wj(s), f_U=A_U(u)+Ls, g_U=μ||u||²/2−L<x,u>+μs²/2+Lz²/2+K. Theorem A.4 proves global curvature/smoothness bounds for sufficiently small βϑ, exact response (u*,s*,z*)=(κx,r(κx)/L,0), and F_U(x)=H_U(κx). Numerical rescaling is required to fit prescribed primitive budgets; do not silently identify μ/2 with μ.

A.4, pp.14–15: set τ=w_J/8, rτ=Rτ(Uᵀb), d=r−rτ, and D=μ(r²−rτ²)/(2L²)−(μ/L)d q_wJ. K0=K−D is the inactive scalar potential. Its informative difference obeys ||∇D||∞≤B. For fresh ξ∼Ber(p), return exact ∇f_U and ∇(g_quad+K0+(ξ/p)D). These are gradients of globally defined C³ scalar functions, with conditional mean ∇g_U and variance (p^−1−1)||∇D||²≤σ_g². Individual sample convexity or sample smoothness bounds are not required by Definition 3.2.

A.5, pp.15–16: make public in the stronger genie transcript all projections of hidden columns onto inserted query directions, together with fully revealed columns. Scalar coefficients are therefore accounted for. Lemma A.5 bounds unrevealed projections: b*²=8log(4MT/δ0)/(d−M−T−2), TMb*²≤1/2 imply ||P_V U_i||²≤2Mb*² with probability ≥1−δ0. A sufficient d is C(M+T)ϑ²T log(4MT/δ0). Insert both x,u per call and the fixed output direction, giving M≤2N+1. On the good event virtual and actual transcripts agree; a nonactivation reveals no new column and activation exposes at most one.

Theorem A.6, p.16: for N≤T/(16p), use δ0=1/8; complete revelations are dominated by Binomial(N,p). With probability ≥13/16, the terminal column remains hidden and output gradient norm is ≥8ε. Average over the frame and oracle and then fix a hard instance. The source separately converts fixed-horizon hardness to worst-instance expected query hardness by truncation and Markov bounds. Its statement has numerical c,C, L,Δ>0, σ_g≥0, κ≥2, 1≤ϑ≤κ, 0<ε≤c min{L,κsqrt(LΔ)}, and sufficiently large dimension. Taking ϑ comparable to χ in the positive-variation budget window yields equation (31).
content.required_inputs: A bounded-gradient zero-chain with finite gap and frontier gradient separation; flat C³ masks with dimension-uniform derivative bounds; a Haar orthonormal frame; global primitive smoothness and strong-convexity budgets. Imported source interfaces are Lemmas A.1–A.3, Theorem A.4 and Lemma A.5, read in this PDF but not independently reproved here.
transfer_obligations: Re-establish each imported residual, flattening, exact-response and projection interface for a modified construction; this recipe alone proves none of them.

Verify global budgets, numerical rescaling, finite initial gap and βϑ smallness simultaneously. Preserve the source accuracy window, including any extra smallness needed when fitting a prescribed ρ budget.
Account for exact scalar coefficients, arbitrary query magnitudes and arbitrary measurable terminal outputs; a zero-chain support argument alone is insufficient.
Respect separate fixed-horizon and worst-instance expected call statements; no universal 2/3 success or all-path stopping cap is supplied.
For normalized χ dependence require ρ≳μ and χ≲κ. Matching χ²κ⁸ with the upper bound additionally needs the curvature-controlled subclass; the general upper coefficient is χ³κ⁸.
